The position requires close attention to documentation, shipment schedules, payments, customs procedures, logistics coordination, and costs. The selected candidate will not only track shipments but will also ensure that the documentation and financial information associated with imports are accurate and properly processed. Job Details Category Details Company Fatima Group Position Assistant Manager – Import (Steel) Department/Area Import / Procurement / Supply Chain Education Master’s degree in Business Administration & Supply Chain Management Experience 3–5 years of relevant procurement experience Preferred Background Manufacturing or industrial environment Job Level Assistant Manager Specialization Import Operations, Steel Procurement & Supply Chain What Does an Assistant Manager – Import (Steel) Do? An Assistant Manager – Import (Steel) is responsible for making sure that imported materials move smoothly from overseas suppliers to the organization. The position involves much more than simply placing purchase orders. The employee must coordinate international suppliers, freight forwarders, shipping lines, clearing agents, banks, and internal departments . A successful professional must understand how an international shipment progresses from supplier dispatch through shipping, documentation, customs clearance, and final delivery. The role also involves financial analysis. Import professionals need to understand different pricing arrangements such as FOB, CFR, and CIF , while calculating freight, duties, taxes, port charges, and other costs to determine the actual landed cost of imported material. Key Responsibilities Manage Import Operations One of the primary responsibilities will be to manage import operations from shipment initiation through delivery . This includes tracking shipments and monitoring their progress to ensure materials arrive according to the required schedule. The Assistant Manager Will Also Be Responsible For Related Shipment tracking Jobs Import documentation Processing activities Landed-cost calculations ERP transactions Delivery coordination Effective shipment tracking is particularly important for industrial organizations because delays in imported materials can affect production schedules, inventory levels, and business operations. Handle Import Documentation International imports involve a significant amount of documentation. The successful candidate will be expected to understand and manage important import documents and procedures. These Include Letter of Credit (LC) TT / Advance Payment Commercial invoices Packing lists Bill of Lading (B/L) Certificates of Origin Insurance documents Customs documentation The candidate should be comfortable checking documentation for accuracy and ensuring that required documents are available at the appropriate stage of the import process. Errors or missing information can lead to shipment delays, additional charges, or customs-related complications, making documentation management a critical part of this position. Coordinate With Overseas Suppliers The Assistant Manager will communicate with overseas suppliers to ensure that shipments are prepared and dispatched according to agreed requirements. Supplier coordination can involve confirming shipment details, following up on documents, monitoring dispatch schedules, and addressing issues that may affect delivery. Strong communication skills will therefore be important for the successful candidate. Work With Freight Forwarders and Shipping Lines Import operations require close coordination with logistics partners. The Selected Candidate Will Coordinate With Freight forwarders Job Listings Shipping lines Clearing agents Banks Overseas suppliers Internal departments The objective is to ensure that shipments are handled efficiently and cleared without unnecessary delays. FOB (Free on Board) generally means the seller’s responsibility covers the goods up to the specified point of shipment, while certain transportation and subsequent costs are handled by the buyer. CFR (Cost and Freight) generally includes the cost of goods and freight to the destination port, while insurance is not included in the CFR price. CIF (Cost, Insurance and Freight) generally includes the cost of goods, freight, and marine insurance to the destination port.
